'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Russo-Ukrainian War]]
**[[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
***[[Kyiv offensive (2022)|Kyiv offensive]]
****[[Battle of Kyiv (2022)|Battle of Kyiv]]
*****The [[Kyiv]] city government and [[Kyiv Oblast]] administration impose a 35-hour curfew starting at 20:00 [[UTC+2|local time]] (18:00 [[UTC]]). [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/kyiv-struck-by-russian-shelling-ukraine-says-least-two-killed-2022-03-15/ (Reuters)] 
****[[Fox News]] cameraman Pierre Zakrzewski and producer Oleksandra Kuvshynova are killed, and [[war correspondent]] [[Benjamin Hall (journalist)|Benjamin Hall]] is injured, while covering the fighting between [[Russian Ground Forces|Russian]] and [[Ukrainian Ground Forces|Ukrainian forces]] in Horenka, Kyiv Oblast. [https://www.theguardian.com/media/2022/mar/15/fox-news-cameraman-killed-ukraine-pierre-zakrzewski (''The Guardian'')]
***[[Eastern Ukraine offensive]]
****[[Siege of Mariupol]]
*****Around 2,000 private cars have left [[Mariupol]] since a [[humanitarian corridor]] was imposed, with another 2,000 cars waiting to leave. [https://www.deccanherald.com/amp/international/world-news-politics/2000-cars-left-ukraines-mariupol-via-humanitarian-corridor-1091563.html (''Deccan Herald'')]
*****Russian troops storm the [[Mariupol regional intensive care hospital]] and take around 400 people hostage. Local authorities confirm that the damaged hospital is now under Russian control. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-60757133 (BBC News)]
***[[Southern Ukraine offensive]]
****The [[Ministry of Defence (Russia)|Russian Defence Ministry]] says that its forces have taken full control of Ukraine's [[Kherson Oblast]] and that they destroyed six [[Ukrainian Air Force]] jets, seven helicopters, and 13 [[UAV]]s in the last 24 hours. [https://nation.com.pk/2022/03/15/russia-says-it-takes-control-of-ukraines-entire-kherson-region/ (''The Nation'')]
****[[Satellite imagery|Satellite images]] from [[Planet Labs]] appear to show multiple Russian helicopters burning at [[Kherson International Airport]] after Ukrainian forces said they struck the airport. This is the second major Ukrainian attack on the facility since it fell to Russian forces on 2 March. [https://www.thedrive.com/the-war-zone/44780/ukraine-strikes-back-barrage-leaves-russian-occupied-kherson-airbase-in-flames (''The Drive'')] [https://edition.cnn.com/europe/live-news/ukraine-russia-putin-news-03-15-22/index.html (CNN)]
***[[Ukrainian refugee crisis]]
****The [[United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees]] says that over three million people have now fled Ukraine since the invasion began. [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/europe/ukraine-war-three-million-refugees-russia-b2036678.html (''The Independent'')]
*[[Israeli–Palestinian conflict]]
**Two [[Palestinians]] are shot and killed in clashes with [[Israeli security forces|Israeli forces]] in the [[West Bank]], according to Palestinian sources. A man is also killed in the [[Negev Bedouin|Bedouin]] town of [[Rahat]] in the [[Negev]] following clashes with members of the [[Israel Border Police|Border Police]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2022/3/15/several-palestinians-including-teen-killed-by-israeli-forces (Al Jazeera)] [https://www.jpost.com/breaking-news/article-701326 (''The Jerusalem Post'')]

'''Arts and culture'''
*Burkinabè architect [[Diébédo Francis Kéré]] wins the 2022 [[Pritzker Architecture Prize]], becoming the first African and black person to do so. [https://www.theguardian.com/artanddesign/2022/mar/15/it-is-unbelievable-francis-kere-becomes-first-black-architect-to-win-the-pritzker-prize (''The Guardian'')]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Puerto Rican government-debt crisis]]
**[[Puerto Rico]] exits out of [[bankruptcy]] after completing the largest public debt restructuring in U.S. history. [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/amp/rcna20054 (NBC News)]
*[[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Joe Biden]] signs a $1.5 trillion budget bill, which includes $13.6 billion in aid for Ukraine. [https://thehill.com/homenews/administration/598074-biden-signs-15-government-funding-bill-with-ukraine-aid (''The Hill'')]
*The [[United Kingdom]]'s [[Gambling Commission]] awards the next licence to run the [[National Lottery (United Kingdom)|National Lottery]] to [[Czech Republic|Czech]]-owned lottery operator Allwyn Entertainment Ltd, replacing [[Camelot Group]] which has operated the lottery since it was started in [[1994 in the United Kingdom|1994]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/business-60733391 (BBC News)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[University_of_the_Southwest#2022_pick-up_truck_accident|University of the Southwest pick-up truck accident]]
** Nine people die in a head-on collision between a [[pickup truck]] and a van carrying members of the [[University of the Southwest]] men's and women's golf teams in [[Andrews County, Texas]], United States. Six students and a faculty member are killed in the team vehicle, with two other students airlifted to a hospital in [[Lubbock, Texas]] in critical condition. The driver of the pickup and its passenger also die. [https://www.espn.com/college-sports/story/_/id/33516134/multiple-dead-crash-involving-university-southwest-golf-team (ESPN)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil]]
***[[Brazil]] reports its first two cases of the [[Deltacron]] variant in the [[North Region, Brazil|Northern states]] of Pará and Amapá. [https://brazilian.report/liveblog/2022/03/15/deltacron-variant/ (''The Brazilian Report'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in mainland China]]
***[[China]] reports a record 5,280 new [[COVID-19]] cases in the past 24 hours. [https://www.straitstimes.com/asia/east-asia/china-reports-sharp-rise-in-covid-19-cases (''The Straits Times'')] [https://www.ndtv.com/world-news/china-records-5-280-new-covid-19-cases-highest-in-2-years-2823192 (NDTV)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Namibia]]
***[[Namibia]] drops its requirement of [[Face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic|face mask]] and mandatory [[Polymerase chain reaction|PCR]] [[COVID-19 test]] for vaccinated visitors as the number of cases falls. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/masks-pcr-tests-no-longer-needed-namibia-covid-cases-fall-2022-03-15/ (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[Second Gentleman of the United States|Second Gentleman]] [[Doug Emhoff]] tests positive for COVID-19. [https://www.npr.org/2022/03/15/1086790648/second-gentleman-doug-emhoff-tests-positive-for-covid-19 (NPR)]
 
'''International relations'''
*[[Reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[Russia–Ukraine relations]]
***The fourth round of talks between the [[Russia]]n and [[Ukraine|Ukrainian]] delegations resumes a day after talks were suspended for technical reasons. [https://www.thequint.com/amp/story/news/world/ukraine-russia-war-invasion-putin-zelenskyy (''The Quint'')] [https://www.cbsnews.com/video/peace-talks-resume-as-russia-continues-assault-on-ukraine-cities/ (CBS News)]
***Ukrainian presidential aide Mykhailo Podolyak reaffirms that ceasefire negotiations are ongoing. [https://www.freepressjournal.in/world/russia-ukraine-conflict-talks-resume-negotiations-are-ongoing-says-kyiv-negotiator (''The Free Press Journal'')]
***Podolyak says that talks between Ukraine and Russia are difficult but also says that there is "certainly room for compromise". Talks between both countries will continue tomorrow. [https://apnews.com/article/russia-ukraine-kyiv-business-global-trade-europe-d3fc8e510956c63a8d7b53efb8700c9e (AP)] [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/ukraine-official-says-russia-talks-are-very-difficult-sees-room-compromise-2022-03-15/ (Reuters)]
**[[Ukraine–European Union relations]]
***The [[Prime Minister of Poland|prime ministers of Poland]], [[Prime Minister of Slovenia|Slovenia]], and the [[Prime Minister of the Czech Republic|Czech Republic]] travel to [[Kyiv]] by train to meet with [[President of Ukraine|Ukrainian President]] [[Volodymyr Zelenskyy]] and [[Prime Minister of Ukraine|Prime Minister]] [[Denys Shmyhal]] in order to demonstrate "unequivocal support" of the [[European Union]] for the sovereignty and independence of Ukraine. [https://www.cnn.com/europe/live-news/ukraine-russia-putin-news-03-15-22/h_cba7fe20200bbd64f6841feea8db4225 (CNN)]
**[[International sanctions during the Russo-Ukrainian War]]
***[[Russia–United States relations]]
****[[Russia]] sanctions U.S. President [[Joe Biden]], [[United States Secretary of State|Secretary of State]] [[Antony Blinken]], [[United States Secretary of Defense|Secretary of Defense]] [[Lloyd Austin]], [[Director of the Central Intelligence Agency|CIA Director]] [[William J. Burns (diplomat)|William Burns]], and former Secretary of State [[Hillary Clinton]] in response to United States sanctions on Russian officials. [https://news.sky.com/story/ukraine-war-joe-biden-and-senior-white-house-officials-sanctioned-by-russia-12566853 (Sky News)]
***[[Canada–Russia relations]]
****Russia sanctions [[Prime Minister of Canada|Canadian Prime Minister]] [[Justin Trudeau]], [[Minister of Foreign Affairs (Canada)|Foreign Affairs Minister]] [[Mélanie Joly]], General [[Wayne Eyre]] and most members of the [[Parliament of Canada|Canadian parliament]]. All those sanctioned are banned from entering Russia. [https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/russia-black-list-trudeau-joly-anand-1.6385573 (CBC News)]
***[[Russia–Spain relations]]
****[[Law enforcement in Spain|Spanish police]] seize a [[superyacht]] at the [[Port of Barcelona]] which is owned by [[Russian oligarch]] [[Sergey Chemezov]], after Chemezov was sanctioned by the [[European Union]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/spain-seizes-russian-oligarchs-yacht-barcelona-2022-03-14/ (Reuters)]
***[[Belarus–United States relations]]
****The United States imposes additional sanctions on [[President of Belarus|Belarusian President]] [[Alexander Lukashenko]]. [https://amp.cnn.com/cnn/2022/03/15/politics/united-states-belarus-sanctions/index.html (CNN)]
**[[Enlargement of NATO]]
***[[President of Ukraine|Ukrainian President]] [[Volodymyr Zelenskyy]] acknowledges that [[Ukraine]] will not be able to join [[NATO]]. [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/europe/zelensky-ukraine-conflict-nato-b2036280.html?amp (''The Independent'')]
**[[Russia in the Council of Europe]]
***Russia formally withdraws from the [[Council of Europe]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/russia-formally-quits-council-europe-rights-watchdog-2022-03-15 (Reuters)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2022 Karnataka hijab row]]
**In [[India]], the [[Karnataka High Court]] upholds restrictions on the wearing of the [[hijab]] in its schools, with Chief Justice [[Ritu Raj Awasthi]] saying in the court's judgement that the wearing of the hijab "does not form a part of essential religious practice in Islamic faith." [https://www.reuters.com/world/india/india-court-upholds-karnataka-states-ban-hijab-class-2022-03-15/ (Reuters)]
*[[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[Illia Kyva]], a politician for the pro-Russian [[Opposition Platform — For Life]], is deprived of his MP status in the [[Verkhovna Rada]], Ukraine's parliament. A further four MPs quit the party. [https://en.interfax.com.ua/news/general/813750.html (Interfax Ukraine)]
*[[2022 Northeastern U.S. serial shooter]]
**The [[Metropolitan Police Department of the District of Columbia|DC Police Department]] arrest a suspected [[serial killer]] involved in the murders of two [[Homelessness in the United States|homeless]] men, and the attempted murder of three others in [[Washington, D.C.]] and [[New York City]]. [https://nypost.com/2022/03/15/suspect-in-deadly-shooting-spree-of-dc-nyc-homeless-people-arrested/ (''New York Post'')]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[War crimes in the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
***The [[United States Senate]] unanimously passes a bipartisan resolution declaring [[President of Russia|Russian President]] [[Vladimir Putin]] a [[War crime|war criminal]], and calls for his investigation by the [[International Criminal Court]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/us/us-senate-unanimously-condemns-putin-war-criminal-2022-03-15/ (Reuters)]
*[[2022 Turkmenistan presidential election]]
**[[Serdar Berdimuhamedow]] is elected [[President of Turkmenistan]], succeeding his father [[Gurbanguly Berdimuhamedow]]. [https://apnews.com/article/central-asia-asia-turkmenistan-presidential-elections-elections-3d13e95fe055bf53525141c351708488 (AP)]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[Intel]] pledges €33 billion in investments in the [[European Union]] factories and research facilities, including €17 billion for building a chip-making plant in [[Magdeburg]], [[Germany]] and €12 billion for upgrading the [[Republic of Ireland|Irish]] [[Intel Ireland|plant]]; the company promises €80 billion over the next decade for the EU. [https://www.zdnet.com/article/intel-to-spend-eur33-billion-on-new-eu-fabs-r-d-expansions/ (ZDNet)]
